Anonymous commented on  SPARKR-1 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-1>

Re: Data Frame abstraction layer for RDD <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-1>

DDF project uses SQL mapping or extract RDD and work on RDD so they have flexibility. The idea is that when you are doing simple SQL like manipulations, by mapping them to SQL one can unleash the query optimizer, for instance changing the order of a where vs a select. If select and where are implemented as R functions, those would be black box to any optimizer I can think of. On the other hand one in R may do thing like group data by user-id and then fit a linear model to each group and I don't think you can do that by SQL mapping, unless UDF have become more powerful since I last checked. I wrote a package to support data frames on top of sparkR where the goal was to show the API possibilities more than utter efficiency – will not work well for small reduce groups. See RevolutionAnalytics/plyrmr on github. Originally developed for Hadoop MR now has a partial spark backend. You all know what has been said about premature optimization. I think mapping to SQL is premature optimization. First implement, say, filter, like plyrmr does, executing R functions on chunks of data. Then map the simple case to SQL for max speed, transparently for user. Doing only SQL operations in R is not in keeping with the statistical focus of the language IMHO.

Anonymous commented on  SPARKR-144 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-144>

Re: Implement saveAsTextFile() in the RDD class <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-144>

I've looked at the recent work on `saveAsTextFile()` - glad to see progress being made here!

It appears that the current approach is to serialize to a string on the R side rather than Java. If we want to do that, it would be most useful if we can represent any arbitrary R object as a record in the text file. I modified the "saveAsTextFile" branch for this feature to do so.

I removed `toString()`, whose purpose in R is for printing, and will very quickly get us into trouble (anything outside of simple types, character vectors with newline characters in them, etc.), and replaced it with a base64 encoding of the a raw serialized representation of the object.

I also added a function `textObjectFile()`, which behaves like `textFile()`, except that it also deserializes the data so that you are dealing with your native R objects again.

I also added a unit test to illustrate how it is used and expected to behave. I don't know if this is what you have in mind, but it's moving toward the type of thing I've been looking for - a way to permanently store results of analysis (including more complex R objects) that may be too large to `collect()` in a way that I can load back in as an RDD exactly the way it was before I wrote it.

Since I'm not familiar with your PR protocol, and since I did this without discussing and it may not be exactly what you want, I'll provide a link to the code comparison instead of a PR:

https://github.com/hafen/SparkR-pkg/compare/sun-rui:saveAsTextFile...saveAsTextFile-serialize

I'm happy to PR and discuss changes from there.

Develop a serializer&deserializer which can serialize Java objects to R objects and deserialize Java objects from R objects (Something like the Java pickler&unpickler used by PySpark). This feature provides the foundation for further developments, such as MLLib integration, read from and save as Hadoop files whose content is in Java data types that can be recognized by JVM languages, etc.

In the long term, the serde may be implemented by directly parsing/generating R objects.

cd /root

R CMD javareconf
tar xvzf rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz; R CMD INSTALL rJava
/root/spark/sbin/slaves.sh R CMD javareconf; R CMD INSTALL ~/rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz

cd /root
git clone https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg.git
cd SparkR-pkg

messages.body_plain:
I'm having a problem that arises with a Spark 1.1.1 cluster but not a
Spark 1.1.0 cluster.

I start a Spark cluster via the ec2 script and login to the master node.

Then I set up SparkR as follows.

echo '#!/bin/bash' > /usr/bin/realpath
echo 'readlink -e $1' >> /usr/bin/realpath
chmod guo+x /usr/bin/realpath

cd /root
wget http://cran.cnr.berkeley.edu/src/contrib/rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz
/root/spark-ec2/copy-dir rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz
R CMD javareconf
tar xvzf rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz; R CMD INSTALL rJava
/root/spark-ec2/copy-dir /usr/bin/realpath
/root/spark/sbin/slaves.sh R CMD javareconf
/root/spark/sbin/slaves.sh R CMD INSTALL ~/rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz

cd /root
git clone https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg.git
cd SparkR-pkg
./install-dev.sh
/root/spark-ec2/copy-dir /root/SparkR-pkg

Next I create a simple test file and put it on HDFS.

echo "1" > /tmp/file.csv
echo "1" >> /tmp/file.csv
echo "1" >> /tmp/file.csv
echo "1" >> /tmp/file.csv
echo "1" >> /tmp/file.csv
export PATH=$PATH:/root/ephemeral-hdfs/bin/
hadoop fs -mkdir /data/test
hadoop fs -copyFromLocal /tmp/file.csv /data/test

Now I start SparkR and read the file and count the lines.

cd /root/SparkR-pkg
MASTER=`cat /root/spark-ec2/cluster-url` SPARK_MEM=6g ./sparkR

# following lines in R:
hdfs_master <- system("cat /root/ephemeral-hdfs/conf/masters", intern = TRUE)
lines <- textFile(sc, paste0("hdfs://", hdfs_master, ":9000/data/test"))
count(lines)

On Spark 1.1.0, this returns 5 as it should. On Spark 1.1.1 I get a
slew of Java error messages (see attached).

-chris

SparkR <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR> /  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-164> SPARKR-164 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-164>
Temporary files used by SparkR accumulat as time goes on <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-164>
Issue Type:    Bug
Assignee:   Sun Rui <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=sunrui>
Components:   Internals
Created:   29/Dec/14 7:19 PM
Priority:    Major
Reporter:   Sun Rui <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=sunrui>

As reported in https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/pull/125, "after long-time executions, SparkR jobs left too many temporary files which take a lot of space in /tmp".

This was introduced when using temporary file instead of stdin to feed data from RRDD to R worker. Refer to https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-113 and https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/pull/94

We need to delete the temporary file after it was used.
